### 5.8 Personalization and extensibility

| Tool | Applies to | Can do | Can't do or notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| User personalization | Any page | Saved searches, column widths, home icons, infolets; Redwood pages remember column order. 26D: Redwood Purchasing (opt-in) and Supplier Model tables keep layouts server-side. | Affects only you; leave any sandbox first. |
| Sandboxes (Navigator > Configuration > Sandboxes) | All configuration tools | Isolate, preview, publish; Migration UI moves changes between environments | Publish or delete before each update. Job-role layers need a sandbox with only Page Composer. |
| Page Composer (Settings and Actions > Edit Pages) | Classic ADF pages | Add, hide, move components; required or read-only; layout; saved searches for others; flexfield attributes on a page | Can't change data or functional security, filter or reorder lists of values, add code or validation logic, call other APIs, change the Navigator, or configure the Search region of Search and Select dialogs. |
| Visual Builder Studio (Edit Page in Visual Builder Studio) | Redwood pages | Business rules to show, hide, require or default fields; rearrange fields; page constants; 26D announcement banners | Procurement advises Express mode. The guide *Extending Redwood Applications for HCM and SCM Using Visual Builder Studio* is in the Procurement and SCM book lists, not Financials. |
| Guided journeys | Redwood pages, Supplier Portal | Attach tutorials and policies to pages | External supplier users need extra setup |
| Application Composer | "Certain applications" only | Fields, objects, foreign-key relationships, subtabs, triggers and validation rules, custom subject areas | The Application Composer guide covers Sales, Service, Supply Chain Management and Project Management applications, not Financials; use flexfields for Payables and Receivables (verify in your pod). |
| Flexfields | Most business objects | Descriptive (base table), extensible (extension table, many contexts), key; Manage Descriptive Flexfields, Manage Extensible Flexfields, Manage Value Sets; deploy | Primary extension path for Payables and Receivables. Order Management: Manage Order Extensible Flexfields. |
| Order Management extensions | Sales orders | Groovy at On Save, On Start of Submission Request, On End of Submission Request (Manage Order Management Extensions) | Nothing runs after fulfillment starts; the last point may change only flexfields. Transformation rules must be rewritten as extensions. |
| Business rules | Order Management, Redwood pages | Processing constraints, approval, assignment and routing rules | Redwood order pages can make Revision Reason or Release Reason required |
| Structure and User Interface Text (Navigator > Configuration); Appearance | Navigator, home, themes, labels | Groups, page entries, quick actions; Redwood themes; replace a term everywhere | Default theme is Redwood with News feed; no new classic themes. |

### 5.10 Productivity tips

- Saved searches: Set as Default and Run Automatically; add them to the Watchlist with Manage Watchlist. Redwood saved searches exist on Purchase Orders, Order Management (25C, shareable with Copy Link), My Requisitions and Self-Service Receiving (26D), but not on the 26D Supplier Portal invoices page.
- Query By Example filters stay applied even when the row is hidden; Clear All removes them.
- Export to Excel takes the selected rows, or all rows if none are selected, within current filters and visible columns.
- Keys: in ADF pages Alt+s saves, Alt+m submits, Alt+c cancels where the letter is underlined; in Redwood tables F2 enters or leaves actionable mode and Esc exits.
- Check the URL (`faces` or `redwood`) before choosing a fix, extension tool or shortcut.
- Bookmark Redwood sales orders; bookmark and share Approvals work area filters.
- Predefined timeouts (not editable): session lifetime 8 hours, idle session 120 minutes, browser inactivity 30 minutes; some pages differ. Sign in once, in one tab of one browser.
- Show Help Icons for page help; Record Issue for the help desk (Redwood pages from 26D); Transaction Console for stuck approvals.

## 6. REST APIs for P2P and O2C

REST is the interactive integration layer of Fusion: one record or a small set of records per call, synchronous validation, and custom actions that run business actions such as invoice validation or hold release. Do not assume UI behaviour: Oracle notes that cascade defaulting from the Create or Edit Invoice pages does not happen on a REST update of a Payables invoice ([Points to Consider](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Points_to_Consider.html)). Use FBDI and scheduled processes (section 7) for volume, OTBI and BICC (section 8) for reporting, and REST for lookups, single transactions, status checks and agent tools (sections 10 and 11). This section is built from the 26D *All REST Endpoints* lists of the Financials (farfa), Procurement (fapra), SCM (fasrp), Common Features (farca) and CX Sales and Fusion Service (faaps) guides. The 26D SCM library links to the SCM REST guide published as 26C; SCM rows and examples use that edition. Appendix C lists every root resource cited here.

### 6.1 Conventions

Table 6-1. Rules that apply to every resource in this section.

| Topic | Rule in 26D | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Base URL | `https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/<resource>` for Financials, Procurement and SCM. CX resources such as `accounts` and `hubOrganizations` use `https://<POD_HOST>/crmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/<resource>`. A path without a version returns 404; Oracle recommends 11.13.18.05 (some Oracle examples use `latest`). | [URL Paths](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/URL_Paths_for_REST_Services.html) |
| Spectra (v1) resources | `https://<POD_HOST>/api/boss/data/objects/<module>/v1/<service>`; query with `$filter`, `$limit`, `$offset`, `$sortBy`, `$fields`; every Spectra resource needs an OAuth token from OCI IAM. ERP Document IO and ERP Data Integrations use a separate `/api/erp/integrations/resources/v1/...` pattern (see 6.2 and 6.4). | [Quick Start](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Quick_Start.html), [Manage Collections](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Collections.html) |
| Authentication | OWSM policy accepts Basic over SSL, SAML 2.0 bearer, JWT (passes the user name only) and OAuth 2.0 tokens from the OCI IAM identity domain. Fusion paths accept the Authorization Code, Authorization Code with PKCE and JWT User Assertion grants; Client Credentials works only for Spectra `/api/...` resources. | [Quick Start](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Quick_Start.html), [Configure OAuth](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/configure_oauth.html), [JWT](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Use_JWT_Token_for_Authorization.html) |
| Media types | POST, PATCH: `Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json` (or `application/json`). Custom action: `application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json`, result `application/vnd.oracle.adf.actionresult+json`. Batch: `application/vnd.oracle.adf.batch+json`. Send `Accept: application/json`. | [Media Types](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Media_Types.html) |
| Framework version | Header `REST-Framework-Version: <1-9>`. Without it the server uses the API default (version 1 unless the API declares another); `GET https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/` shows `defaultFrameworkVersion` and `allowedFrameworkVersions`. Versions are not backward compatible: 2 RowMatch `q` with child filters and UPPER; 3 nested children returned as paged collections; 4 structured errors (`o:errorCode`, `o:errorPath`); 5 typed custom-method results, some dependent LOVs become roots; 6 item metadata in `@context`; 7 row-level LOVs hidden; 8 CLOB as plain text, multi-select values as arrays, encoded keys; 9 high-precision numbers as strings, 404 for disabled accessors, backslash escape in LIKE. | [Set the REST Framework Version](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Setting_the_REST_Framework_Version.html) |
| Child resources and keys | `/<root>/{key}/child/<child>/{key}`. A key can be a primary, alternate or hashed composite key; take it from the `self` link instead of building it. For composite keys (invoice lines, installments) query the child collection with `q` on the key columns. Never send both a generated ID and its user key (for example `InvoiceId` and `InvoiceNumber`) in one payload. | [HTTP Methods](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Resource_Methods.html), [Points to Consider](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Points_to_Consider.html), [Quick Start](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Quick_Start.html) |
| Custom actions | `POST /<root>/{key}/action/<name>` (item level) or `POST /<root>/action/<name>` (collection level, marked (C) in 6.2 to 6.4) with action+json. When the URL names the action, the body holds only its parameters. | [Custom Actions](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/custom-actions.html) |
| Metadata | `GET <base>/<resource>/describe` returns attributes (type, mandatory, updatable, queryable), finders, child and LOV links and actions; `<base>/describe?metadataMode=list` or `metadataMode=minimal` covers the whole catalog (`<base>` = `https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05`). `Accept: application/vnd.oracle.openapi3+json` returns OpenAPI; `Accept-Language` translates labels. Filtering on an attribute with `queryable: false` returns 400. | [Access Metadata](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Use_Metadata_Catalog.html), [Manage Collections](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Collections.html) |
| List of values | LOV roots (titled *List of Values*, most ending in `LOV`): 115 in Financials, 35 in Procurement, 227 in SCM; a few more roots end in `LOV` under other titles. Row-level LOVs appear as `.../{key}/lov/<name>` links and are hidden from version 7. Use `finder` or `q` on LOV roots and `dependency=` for dependent LOVs. Cross-pillar LOV access uses the orphan privileges Get Enterprise Structures Using REST API and Get General Ledger Setups Using REST API. | [Framework Version](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Setting_the_REST_Framework_Version.html), [LOV Privileges](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/LOV_REST_API_Privileges.html), [Enterprise Structures](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Get_Enterprise_Structures_Using_REST_API.html) |
| Flexfields | DFF and GDF values are child resources: `invoiceDff`, `invoiceLineDff`, `invoiceDistributionDff`, `invoiceGdf`, `receivablesInvoiceDFF`, `standardReceiptDFF`, `invoiceHoldDff`, and `DFF` or `globalDFF` on procurement and SCM resources. The context is the attribute `__FLEX_Context`; each segment is an attribute of the child (check names with `describe`). LOV roots `FlexFndDffDescriptiveFlexfieldContexts` and `FlexFndPvsCharacterIdCharacterValues` list contexts and values. | resource pages in the endpoint lists |
| Attachments | Child `attachments` (some resources use another name, such as `batchAttachment`). Create with `DatatypeCode` FILE plus Base64 `FileContents`, TEXT plus `UploadedText`, or WEB_PAGE plus `Url`, and a `CategoryName`; download through the `FileContents` enclosure link. | [Work with Attachments](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Work_with_Attachments.html) |
| Batch | POST to the version root with batch+json and a `parts` array (Oracle's examples post to `https://<POD_HOST>/crmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05`; for Financials, Procurement and SCM resources use the `fscmRestApi` version root, verify in your pod); each part has `id`, relative `path`, `operation` (get, create, update, replace, delete) and optional `payload`. All or nothing: one failing part fails the batch and only failing parts are returned. Some custom actions are not enabled for batch. | [Batch Actions](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Batch_Actions.html) |
| Upsert | POST with header `Upsert-Mode: true` updates the matching record or creates a new one; the payload still needs the attributes mandatory for create. | [HTTP Methods](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Resource_Methods.html) |
| Concurrency | Read the `ETag` header (inside `@context` from version 6). PATCH with `If-Match` returns 412 if the record changed; GET with `If-None-Match` returns 304 if unchanged. Singular resources only. | [ETag](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/verify_your_resource_using_the_etag_value.html) |
| Status codes | 200 OK; 201 Created with `Location`; 202 Accepted (asynchronous, poll the `Location` job); 400 validation error or non-queryable filter; 401 credentials; 403 missing role or privilege (or access from a location blocked by export rules); 404 unknown URI; 405 method not allowed; 406 or 415 wrong Accept or Content-Type; 500 server error; 503 or 504 overload or gateway timeout. From version 4 the error body has `title`, `status` and `o:errorDetails` with `detail`, `o:errorCode`, `o:errorPath`. | [Status Codes](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Status_Codes.html) |
| Privileges | Every operation checks a function privilege and data security; a 403 means the role lacks one. Examples: Purchase Orders GET needs View Purchase Order plus procurement-agent or BU data access; Suppliers needs View Supplier (GET) or Maintain Supplier (POST, PATCH); Sales Orders for Order Hub needs `FOM_SALES_ORDER_REST_GET_PRIV` (GET) or `FOM_SALES_ORDER_REST_POST_PRIV` (POST), and applyHold adds `FOM_APPLY_UPDATE_HOLDS_PRIV` and Manage Orchestration Order Modification; Standard Receipts has separate privileges for POST and for GET or DELETE. Procurement REST Service Duty (`ORA_PO_PROCUREMENT_REST_SERVICE_DUTY`) is for application-to-application integration only and sees all data. See section 12. | [Procurement Privileges](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/procurement/26d/fapra/Roles_and_Privileges.html), [SCM Privileges](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/26c/fasrp/Roles_and_Privileges.html), [Standard Receipts](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Get_Started_Standard_Receipts.html) |
| Opt-in features | Some resources and attributes work only after the related feature is opted in; the `features` resource returns each feature's `EnabledFlag`. | [Quick Start](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Quick_Start.html) |

Table 6-2. Query parameters (collection GET unless noted).

| Parameter | Syntax | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | `q=Supplier='<SUPPLIER>' and StatusCode='OPEN'` | Version 2 and later: `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `LIKE` with `%`, `IN`, `BETWEEN`, `IS NULL`, `UPPER()`, `and`, `or`; child filters such as `invoiceHoldDff.approvedBy='Business'` or `lines.StatusCode='AWAIT_SHIP'`. Version 1 uses semicolon query-by-example (`q=a=1;b=2`). URL-encode spaces and quotes. |
| `finder` | `finder=<Finder>;<var>=<value>,<var2>=<value2>` | Predefined where clause; finder names and variables are on each *Get all* page, for example `PrimaryKey`, `findByOrderNumber`, `invoiceSearch`, `ESSJobStatusRF`. |
| `fields` | `fields=InvoiceNumber,InvoiceAmount;invoiceLines:LineNumber,LineAmount;invoiceLines.invoiceDistributions:DistributionAmount` | Returns only the listed attributes and children (item and collection). If combined with `expand`, only `fields` is applied. |
| `expand` | `expand=lines`, `expand=all`, `expand=invoiceLines.invoiceDistributions` | Includes children; from version 3 they come back as paged collections with `hasMore`. |
| `onlyData` | `onlyData=true` | Drops `links`; cannot be combined with `links`. |
| `limit`, `offset` | `limit=100&offset=200` | Default page size 25; the server can lower it; `offset` is 0-based; continue while `hasMore` is true. |
| `totalResults` | `totalResults=true` | Adds the total match count. |
| `orderBy` | `orderBy=CreationDate:desc,OrderNumber` | Without it paged results are unordered; sort on a unique attribute for stable paging, or page by key (`orderBy=Id&q=Id>'last value'`). |
| `links`, `dependency` | `links=self,canonical`; `dependency=Country=BR` | Filter link relations; pass the driving value of a dependent LOV. |

Sources: [Manage Collections](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Collections.html), [HTTP Methods](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Resource_Methods.html), [Resource Types](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Resource_Types.html).

Safe defaults for scripts and AI agents: GET with `fields` or `onlyData=true`, a `limit` and a finder or key filter; treat every POST, PATCH, DELETE and action as a write that needs approval and an audit trail (sections 11 and 12).

### 6.3 O2C resource catalog

Customer resources are split between books. The party layer of TCA (organizations, persons, addresses, contact points, usages) is exposed in the CX guide under `crmRestApi`; Financials exposes customer account inquiry, and SCM exposes a create-customer service for order capture. None of the root resources in the 26D lists creates customer accounts (HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS), account sites or site uses directly (a negative finding from the endpoint lists). Use the Order Management create-customer service below, the SOAP Customer Account Service operation `mergeCustomerAccount`, which creates an account with its account site and site use for an existing party and party site ([Oracle example](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/sales/oesws/Create-CustomerAccount-including-CustomerAccountSite-and-CustomerAccountSiteUse.html)), or the bulk options in section 7.

| Person party | Hub Persons | `/crmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/hubPersons` | Same pattern; findDuplicates (C) |

| Cash Management | Bank Accounts; Banks; Bank Branches; External Cash Transactions; Cash Bank Account Transfers | `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/cashBankAccounts`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/cashBanks`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/cashBankBranches`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/cashExternalTransactions`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/cashBankAccountTransfers` | Internal bank accounts (bankAccountUses, bankAccountPaymentDocuments); external cash transactions, voided by updating their status |
| Intercompany and netting | Intercompany Agreements; Intercompany Transaction Source Documents; Netting Agreements | `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/intercompanyAgreements`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/intercompanyTransactionSourceDocuments`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/nettingAgreements` | generateTransactions (C), approveTransferAuthorizations (C), generateAccountingLines (C), reverseTransferAuthorizationGrp (C); createTransferAuthorization (C); AP and AR netting rules (nettingSupplierTradingPartners, nettingCustomerTradingPartners) |
| Bulk and jobs | ERP Integrations | `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations` | POST with `OperationName` importBulkData, exportBulkData, uploadFileToUCM or submitESSJobRequest; GET finders ESSJobStatusRF, ESSExecutionDetailsRF, ESSJobExecutionDetailsRF, DocumentRF, DocumentIdsByFilePrefixRF; callback and notification options; example 6.5.10 |
| Bulk and jobs | ERP Processes; ERP Business Events; Analytics | `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpProcesses`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpBusinessEvents`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/analytics` | Process and parameter details; enable or disable business events (section 7); executeLogicalQuery (C) runs an OTBI logical query (section 8) |
| Bulk and jobs | Scheduler; ERP Data Integrations | `ess/rest/scheduler/v1/requests/{requestId}` (Common Features guide); `/api/erp/integrations/resources/v1/{locale}/files/upload` | Job status, cancel, hold and release; Accounting Hub file upload with file and transaction metrics |
| Lookups | Common Lookups; Generic Lookups; Standard Lookups List of Values; Lookups | `commonLookups` and `genericLookups` (Common Features guide, CRUD with child lookupCodes); `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/standardLookupsLOV`; `/crmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/fndStaticLookups` | Lookup views Standard, Common and Set-Enabled; Generic Lookups reads any view. The Common Features guide also lists Spectra versions (Standard Lookups, Common Lookups and Set-Enabled Lookups, Lookup Types and Lookup Codes (Spectra)) |
| Attachments | child `attachments` of each resource | - | See Table 6-1; no root resource |
| Audit | Audit Report | `/fscmRestApi/fndAuditRESTService/audittrail/getaudithistory` (POST) | Audit history by product, business object type, user and event type; fromDate, toDate and product are required; up to one month per request; audit setup operations sit beside it |
| Setup | Features; Setup Tasks | `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/features`; `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/setupTasks` | Opt-in feature status (`EnabledFlag`); setup task metadata, with CSV export and import in `setupTaskCSVExports` and `setupTaskCSVImports` |

### 6.5 Worked examples

Placeholders in angle brackets are environment values. `curl -u "<USER>"` prompts for the password, so no secret is typed on the command line; with OAuth use `-H "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>"` instead. All examples send `REST-Framework-Version: 4` (expanded `q` syntax, nested children as collections, structured errors); lower it if the API's `allowedFrameworkVersions` does not include 4. `-G --data-urlencode` builds an encoded query string. Check every filtered attribute with `describe` (`queryable: true`) before relying on it. Run write examples (6.5.3, 6.5.5, 6.5.7, 6.5.9, 6.5.10) only in a test pod: they create real transactions, approvals and accounting.

#### 6.5.1 Open purchase orders for a supplier

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" -G \
  --data-urlencode "q=Supplier='<SUPPLIER_NAME>' and StatusCode='OPEN'" \
  --data-urlencode "fields=POHeaderId,OrderNumber,Supplier,SupplierSite,ProcurementBU,Status,Ordered,Total,CurrencyCode" \
  --data-urlencode "orderBy=OrderNumber" --data-urlencode "limit=100" \
  --data-urlencode "totalResults=true" --data-urlencode "onlyData=true" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/purchaseOrders"
```

Read `items`, `totalResults` and `hasMore`; repeat with `offset=100`. Lines and schedules are under `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/purchaseOrders/<ORDER_KEY_FROM_SELF_LINK>/child/lines`; take the key from the `self` link. Rows are filtered by data security: buyers see orders of their procurement business units, Payables users see orders of their bill-to business units. Sources: [Get all purchase orders](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/procurement/26d/fapra/op-purchaseorders-get.html), [Procurement Privileges](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/procurement/26d/fapra/Roles_and_Privileges.html).

#### 6.5.2 One invoice with lines, distributions and installments

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" -G \
  --data-urlencode "q=InvoiceNumber='<INVOICE_NUMBER>' and Supplier='<SUPPLIER_NAME>' and BusinessUnit='<BU_NAME>'" \
  --data-urlencode "fields=InvoiceId,InvoiceNumber,InvoiceAmount,ValidationStatus,ApprovalStatus,PaidStatus;invoiceLines:LineNumber,LineType,LineAmount,PurchaseOrderNumber;invoiceLines.invoiceDistributions:DistributionLineNumber,DistributionLineType,DistributionAmount,DistributionCombination;invoiceInstallments:InstallmentNumber,DueDate,UnpaidAmount,HoldFlag" \
  --data-urlencode "onlyData=true" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoices"
```

The same invoice number can exist for more than one supplier, so filter on supplier and business unit as well (Oracle's holds example uses this combination). The only finder on Invoices is PrimaryKey (InvoiceId). Sources: [Get Specific Details example](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Get_Specific_Details_for_Invoices_Lines_Distributions_and_Installments.html), [Get all invoices](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/op-invoices-get.html).

#### 6.5.3 Create an invoice, then validate it

Warning: this creates a real Payables invoice that can be approved, accounted and paid. Use a test pod and a unique invoice number per supplier; a duplicate returns "This invoice number already exists" (AP-810776).

```json
{
  "InvoiceNumber": "<INVOICE_NUMBER>",
  "InvoiceCurrency": "<CURRENCY_CODE>",
  "InvoiceAmount": "<AMOUNT>",
  "InvoiceDate": "<YYYY-MM-DD>",
  "BusinessUnit": "<BU_NAME>",
  "Supplier": "<SUPPLIER_NAME>",
  "SupplierSite": "<SUPPLIER_SITE>",
  "Description": "<DESCRIPTION>",
  "invoiceLines": [
    { "LineNumber": 1, "LineType": "Item", "LineAmount": "<AMOUNT>",
      "DistributionCombination": "<ACCOUNT_COMBINATION>" }
  ]
}
```

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -X POST -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json" -d @invoice.json \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoices"

curl -s -u "<USER>" -X POST -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json" \
  -d '{"InvoiceNumber":"<INVOICE_NUMBER>","BusinessUnit":"<BU_NAME>","Supplier":"<SUPPLIER_NAME>","ProcessAction":"Validate"}' \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoices/action/validateInvoice"
```

A 201 returns `InvoiceId` and the defaulted header. For a PO-matched line replace `DistributionCombination` with `PurchaseOrderNumber`, `PurchaseOrderLineNumber`, `PurchaseOrderScheduleLineNumber`, `Quantity` and `UnitPrice`. Validation returns `{"result": "The current action Validate Invoice has completed successfully."}`; validation calculates tax, checks tolerances and places holds, so check 6.5.4 afterwards. Sources: [PO-matched invoice example](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Create_an_Invoice_with_a_PO_Matched_Line_and_Freight_Line.html), [Unmatched line example](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Create_an_Invoice_with_an_Unmatched_Line_with_Project_Information.html), [Validate an invoice](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/op-invoices-action-validateinvoice-post.html).

#### 6.5.4 Invoices on hold

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" -G \
  --data-urlencode "q=BusinessUnit='<BU_NAME>' and ReleaseName IS NULL" \
  --data-urlencode "fields=HoldId,InvoiceNumber,Supplier,HoldName,HoldReason,HoldDate,LineHeld" \
  --data-urlencode "orderBy=HoldDate:desc" --data-urlencode "onlyData=true" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoiceHolds"
```

Unreleased holds have empty `ReleaseName` and `ReleaseDate`. To release one (write), PATCH `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoiceHolds/<HOLD_ID>` with `{"ReleaseName": "<RELEASE_NAME>"}`; Oracle's example uses the release name "Amount approved". Valid hold and release names come from `payablesInvoiceHoldsLOV` and the row-level LOVs of the hold. Sources: [Holds without unique invoice number](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Get_Holds_Information_for_Invoices_Without_Unique_Invoice_Number.html), [Holds by child attribute](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Get_Invoice_Holds_Using_a_Child_Resource_Attribute.html), [Release an Invoice Hold](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Release_an_Invoice_Hold.html).

#### 6.5.5 Receive a purchase order through receivingReceiptRequests

Warning: this records a real receipt against the purchase order; it feeds receipt accounting and invoice matching and, once delivered, inventory.

```json
{
  "ReceiptSourceCode": "VENDOR",
  "OrganizationCode": "<ORG_CODE>",
  "VendorName": "<SUPPLIER_NAME>",
  "VendorSiteCode": "<SUPPLIER_SITE>",
  "BusinessUnit": "<PROCUREMENT_BU>",
  "EmployeeName": "<RECEIVER_NAME>",
  "lines": [
    { "ReceiptSourceCode": "VENDOR", "SourceDocumentCode": "PO", "TransactionType": "RECEIVE",
      "OrganizationCode": "<ORG_CODE>", "DocumentNumber": "<PO_NUMBER>",
      "DocumentLineNumber": 1, "DocumentShipmentLineNumber": 1,
      "ItemNumber": "<ITEM_NUMBER>", "Quantity": 1, "UnitOfMeasure": "<UOM_NAME>" }
  ]
}
```

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -X POST -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json" -d @receipt.json \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/receivingReceiptRequests"

curl -s -u "<USER>" -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/receivingReceiptRequests/<HEADER_INTERFACE_ID>/child/lines/<INTERFACE_TRANSACTION_ID>/child/processingErrors"
```

With the default `InsertAndProcessFlag` true the request is processed immediately; `ReturnStatus` is SUCCESS or ERROR for synchronous processing (SUBMITTED or QUEUED when asynchronous), `ProcessingStatusCode` is PENDING, ERROR or SUCCESS, and `ReceiptNumber` is returned. With false, rows wait in the interface for the Manage Receiving Transactions scheduled process. `DocumentShipmentLineNumber` (PO schedule) is mandatory for PO receipts. Oracle's examples also pass `AutoTransactCode`, but its attribute description says to leave it blank. Supply `EmployeeId` instead of `EmployeeName` if names are ambiguous. Sources: [Create receipt requests](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/26c/fasrp/op-receivingreceiptrequests-post.html), [Get all receipt requests](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/26c/fasrp/op-receivingreceiptrequests-get.html).

#### 6.5.6 Get a sales order by order number

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" -G \
  --data-urlencode "fields=OrderKey,HeaderId,OrderNumber,SourceTransactionSystem,SourceTransactionId,StatusCode,OnHoldFlag,BuyingPartyName,TransactionalCurrencyCode;lines:FulfillLineId,DisplayLineNumber,ProductNumber,OrderedQuantity,OrderedUOM,StatusCode,ScheduleShipDate,OnHoldFlag;holds:HoldCode,HoldName,ActiveFlag,ApplyDate" \
  --data-urlencode "onlyData=true" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/salesOrdersForOrderHub?finder=findByOrderNumber;OrderNumber='<ORDER_NUMBER>'"
```

Other finders: findBySourceOrderNumberAndSystem (SourceTransactionNumber, SourceTransactionSystem), findByOrderKey (OrderKey = source system, colon, source order ID), findByHeaderId, findByOrderedDate (FromDate, ToDate). The item path uses `OrderKey`: `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/salesOrdersForOrderHub/<ORDER_KEY>/child/lines`. Line-level filters such as `q=lines.StatusCode='AWAIT_SHIP'` need version 2 or later. Sources: [Get all sales orders](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/26c/fasrp/op-salesordersfororderhub-get.html), [SCM Privileges](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/26c/fasrp/Roles_and_Privileges.html).

#### 6.5.7 Apply a hold to a sales order

Warning: a hold stops fulfillment of the order or its lines until released.

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -X POST -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json" \
  -d '{"processRequestOfflineAfter":240,"holdRequests":[{"SourceTransactionSystem":"<SOURCE_SYSTEM>","OrderNumber":"<ORDER_NUMBER>","HoldCode":"<HOLD_CODE>","HoldComments":"<COMMENT>"}]}' \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/salesOrdersForOrderHub/action/applyHold"
```

Take `SourceTransactionSystem` from 6.5.6. Every request needs `SourceTransactionSystem` and `HoldCode` or `HoldName`; a header hold also needs `SourceTransactionId` or `OrderNumber`, a fulfillment line hold needs `FulfillLineId`. Each `result` entry returns `RequestStatus` SUCCESS or ERROR with `Message`. `processRequestOfflineAfter` is the number of seconds after which the call returns and processing continues in the background. Release with `/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/salesOrdersForOrderHub/action/releaseHold` and the same keys plus `HoldReleaseReasonCode` or `HoldReleaseReason`. For many orders post Sales Order Action Requests with `ActionCode` `ORA_FOM_APPLY_ORDER_HOLD`. Sources: [Apply hold](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/26c/fasrp/op-salesordersfororderhub-action-applyhold-post.html), [Release hold](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/26c/fasrp/op-salesordersfororderhub-action-releasehold-post.html).

#### 6.5.8 Open receivables installments for a customer account

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" -G \
  --data-urlencode "fields=AccountId,AccountNumber,CustomerName,TotalOpenReceivablesForAccount;transactionPaymentSchedules:InstallmentId,TransactionNumber,TransactionClass,TransactionDate,PaymentScheduleDueDate,TotalBalanceAmount,EnteredCurrency,InstallmentStatus,PaymentDaysLate" \
  --data-urlencode "onlyData=true" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/receivablesCustomerAccountActivities?finder=CustomerAccountActivitiesFinder;AccountNumber=<ACCOUNT_NUMBER>,TransactionLimitByDays=<DAYS>"

curl -s -u "<USER>" -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" -G \
  --data-urlencode "q=InstallmentStatus='Open'" --data-urlencode "onlyData=true" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/receivablesCustomerAccountActivities/<ACCOUNT_ID>/child/transactionPaymentSchedules"
```

The finder considers transactions up to 90 days past the transaction date unless `TransactionLimitByDays` is set; `TransactionStatus` (Complete or Incomplete) is a further variable. The second call keeps only the open installments of the account found by the first (check in your pod whether the 90-day window also applies to it). Per invoice, use `receivablesInvoices?finder=invoiceSearch;BillToCustomerNumber=<ACCOUNT_NUMBER>,InvoiceStatus=Complete` and read `InvoiceBalanceAmount`. Sources: [Get all customer account activities](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/op-receivablescustomeraccountactivities-get.html), [Site invoices and installments](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Search_for_All_Customer_Site_Invoices_and_Installments.html), [Find Invoices that are Overdue](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Find_Invoices_that_are_Overdue.html).

#### 6.5.9 Create a standard receipt and apply it

Warning: this records customer cash, updates customer balances and creates accounting. Reverse mistakes with `reverseReceipt`; PATCH can change only the customer attributes (CustomerAccountNumber, CustomerBankAccountNumber, CustomerName, CustomerSite).

```json
{
  "ReceiptNumber": "<RECEIPT_NUMBER>",
  "ReceiptMethod": "<RECEIPT_METHOD>",
  "ReceiptDate": "<YYYY-MM-DD>",
  "BusinessUnit": "<BU_NAME>",
  "CustomerAccountNumber": "<ACCOUNT_NUMBER>",
  "CustomerSite": "<BILL_TO_SITE>",
  "Amount": "<AMOUNT>",
  "Currency": "<CURRENCY_CODE>",
  "RemittanceBankAccountNumber": "<REMITTANCE_BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>"
}
```

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -X POST -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json" -d @cash_receipt.json \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/standardReceipts"

curl -s -u "<USER>" -X POST -H "REST-Framework-Version: 4" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json" \
  -d '{"appliedPaymentScheduleId": <INSTALLMENT_ID>, "amountApplied": <AMOUNT>, "calledFrom": "REST"}' \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/standardReceipts/<STANDARD_RECEIPT_ID>/action/applyReceipt"
```

The POST returns `StandardReceiptId`, `State` and `Status`. `appliedPaymentScheduleId` identifies the invoice installment; use the `InstallmentId` from 6.5.8 or from the invoice's `receivablesInvoiceInstallments` (verify in your pod). Without `amountApplied` the full open balance is applied; success returns `{"result": "SUCCESS"}`. Find receipts with `finder=StandardReceiptsFinder;ReceiptNumber=<RECEIPT_NUMBER>`. Prerequisites: customers, Receivables system options, receipt classes and methods, receivables activities. Sources: [Get Started with Standard Receipts](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Get_Started_Standard_Receipts.html), [Create a Standard Receipt](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Create_a_Standard_Receipt.html), [Apply receipt](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/op-standardreceipts-standardreceiptid-action-applyreceipt-post.html), [What fields can I update](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/what-fields-can-i-update-using-the-standard-receipts-rest-api.html).

#### 6.5.10 Submit importBulkData and poll the job

Warning: this loads and imports every row of the file. Build the zip from the FBDI template of the target object (section 7) and Base64-encode it, for example `base64 -w0 <FILE>.zip`.

```json
{
  "OperationName": "importBulkData",
  "DocumentContent": "<BASE64_OF_ZIP>",
  "ContentType": "zip",
  "FileName": "<FILE>.zip",
  "DocumentAccount": "fin$/payables$/import$",
  "JobName": "oracle/apps/ess/financials/payables/invoices/transactions,APXIIMPT",
  "ParameterList": "<PARAMETER_LIST>",
  "CallbackURL": "#NULL",
  "NotificationCode": "10",
  "JobOptions": "InterfaceDetails=1,ImportOption=Y ,PurgeOption = Y,ExtractFileType=ALL"
}
```

```bash
curl -s -u "<USER>" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json" \
  -d @import.json "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations"

curl -s -u "<USER>" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations?finder=ESSJobStatusRF;requestId=<REQUEST_ID>"

curl -s -u "<USER>" \
  "https://<POD_HOST>/fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations?finder=ESSJobExecutionDetailsRF;requestId=<REQUEST_ID>,fileType=ALL"
```

The POST returns `ReqstId`. Poll ESSJobStatusRF until `RequestStatus` reaches a final value (Oracle's example shows SUCCEEDED); ESSExecutionDetailsRF returns the job tree (Load Interface File for Import with child jobs Transfer File and Load File to Interface) as JSON in `RequestStatus`; ESSJobExecutionDetailsRF returns logs and output as a Base64 zip in `DocumentContent`. `JobName` (job package and definition), `DocumentAccount` and `JobOptions` above come from Oracle's Payables invoice import example, whose `ParameterList` is `#NULL,<BU_NAME>,#NULL,#NULL,#NULL,#NULL,#NULL,INVOICE GATEWAY,#NULL,#NULL,#NULL,1,#NULL` (comma-separated in job order, `#NULL` for empty parameters); take the values for other objects from their FBDI template (section 7). Prefer `CallbackURL` or `NotificationCode` to tight polling. For exports, `exportBulkData` runs the report and an Upload Interface Error and Output Details to UCM job, and `getDocumentForDocumentId` (finder DocumentRF) downloads the result. Sources: [POST erpintegrations](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/op-erpintegrations-post.html), [GET erpintegrations](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/op-erpintegrations-get.html), [Get job details (examples)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/op-erpintegrations-operationname-get.html), [Import Financials Data](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Importing_Financials_Data.html), [Export Financials Data](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/financials/26d/farfa/Export_Financials_Data.html).

## 7. Bulk data, SOAP services, scheduled processes and events

This section covers the bulk and asynchronous channels for P2P and O2C: file-based data import (FBDI), the ERP Integration Service, ADFdi workbooks, SOAP services, scheduled processes (Oracle Enterprise Scheduler, ESS) and business events. REST resources are in section 6, BI Publisher, OTBI and BICC extracts in section 8, SQL in section 9, roles and privileges in section 12.

### 7.1 FBDI end to end

FBDI has three parts: an XLSM template per business object, the Load Interface File for Import process that loads the generated CSV files into interface tables, and an object-specific import process that validates the interface rows and creates application data.

| # | Step | UI action (26D) | Automation equivalent (7.4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Get the template | Open the object page in the FBDI guide for Financials, Procurement or SCM. File Links gives the XLSM template (`https://www.oracle.com/webfolder/technetwork/docs/fbdi-26d/fbdi/xlsm/<TEMPLATE>.xlsm`) and its control files. Templates are Windows Excel only. | Generate files with the same layout as the template output. |
| 2 | Prepare data | Fill the worksheets. Keep the column order; hide unused columns, never delete them. Click Generate CSV File on the Instructions and CSV Generation sheet to get a zip. | Zip the CSV files yourself. |
| 3 | Upload | Navigator > Tools > File Import and Export > Actions > Upload. Select the zip and the UCM account of the object (for example `fin/payables/import`), then Save and Close. | `uploadFileToUcm`, or `importBulkData` (upload, load and import in one call). REST writes the account as `fin$/payables$/import$`. |
| 4 | Load | Tools > Scheduled Processes > Schedule New Process > Load Interface File for Import. Required parameters: Import Process, Data File. Child process: Load File to Interface. The parent ends in error if any row fails to load. | `submitESSJobRequest` with job InterfaceLoaderController, or `importBulkData`. |
| 5 | Import | Submit the import process of the object (7.2, 7.3). Valid rows become application data; rejected rows stay in the interface tables and appear in the import report. | `importBulkData` with `ImportOption=Y`, or `submitESSJobRequest` with the import job. |
| 6 | Correct | Load error: all rows already loaded are deleted and the whole batch is rejected; fix the data, regenerate the zip, upload and reload. Import error: read the import log or report, fix the rows with the correction workbook (table below), resubmit the import. | `updateInterfaceData` uploads corrected interface data for an import process and load request ID. |
| 7 | Purge | FBDI interface data older than 30 days is purged automatically per import process. Manually: Purge Interface Tables (Purge Process Intent = File-based data import (FBDI), Maintenance or Other; Import Process; Load Request ID or a load request ID range; optional Extract Data, Allow Context Purge of Data, Number of Days (more than 30, Maintenance only)). Product purges are in 7.7. | `extractAndPurge`; `PurgeOption=Y` in `importBulkData`; `submitESSJobRequest` with job InterfaceLoaderPurge. |

- Job package, job definition and parameter order: Setup and Maintenance > Application Extensions > Manage Enterprise Scheduler Job Definitions and Job Sets for Financial, Supply Chain Management, and Related Applications. Predefined jobs carry an asterisk.
- The Scheduled Processes work area needs a role with the Manage Scheduled Processes privilege. Purge Interface Tables needs the Load Interface File for Import privilege (privilege codes: section 12).

#### Where import errors land and how to fix them

| Import process | Interface tables (main) | Error or rejection table | Correction tool |
|---|---|---|---|
| Import Payables Invoices | AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE, AP_INVOICE_LINES_INTERFACE | AP_INTERFACE_REJECTIONS | Correct Import Errors spreadsheet, then Upload and Import |
| Import AutoInvoice | RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL, RA_INTERFACE_DISTRIBUTIONS_ALL, RA_INTERFACE_SALESCREDITS_ALL, AR_INTERFACE_CONTS_ALL | RA_INTERFACE_ERRORS_ALL | Manage AutoInvoice Lines workbook (Billing work area) or the Import Exceptions infotile, then Save and Run AutoInvoice |
| Process Receipts Through Lockbox | AR_PAYMENTS_INTERFACE_ALL | Lockbox execution report | Manage Lockbox Transmission page: correct or mark for deletion, then Upload |
| Import Orders, Import Blanket Agreements, Import Contract Agreements | PO_HEADERS_INTERFACE, PO_LINES_INTERFACE, PO_LINE_LOCATIONS_INTERFACE, PO_DISTRIBUTIONS_INTERFACE | PO_INTERFACE_ERRORS | Import report; correct the source file and resubmit |
| Import Requisitions | POR_REQ_HEADERS_INTERFACE_ALL, POR_REQ_LINES_INTERFACE_ALL, POR_REQ_DISTS_INTERFACE_ALL | POR_REQ_IMPORT_ERRORS | Correct and reload |
| Import Suppliers and child imports | POZ_SUPPLIERS_INT and the other supplier interface tables (7.2) | POZ_SUPPLIER_INT_REJECTIONS | Job output report; fix the template and reload. Purge: Suppliers work area > Import Suppliers > Actions > Purge Supplier Interface Records |
| Manage Receiving Transactions | RCV_HEADERS_INTERFACE, RCV_TRANSACTIONS_INTERFACE | RCV_INTERFACE_ERRORS | Review Receipts Interface ADFdi workbook (Inventory Management work area task); correct and resubmit |
| Import Trading Community Data in Bulk | Trading Community import tables (7.3) | HZ_IMP_ERRORS | Manage Data Import Batches > batch ID > Edit Data Import Batch > Report |
| Upload Customers | AR_UPD_CUSTOMERS, AR_UPD_CONTACTS, AR_UPD_REF_ACCOUNTS, AR_UPD_BANK_ACCOUNTS | AR_UPD_CUST_ERRORS, AR_UPD_CONTACTS_ERRORS, AR_UPD_REFACCT_ERRORS, AR_UPD_BNKACCT_ERRORS | Correct Customer Data spreadsheet; profile class, payment method, reference account and bank account errors need a new upload |
| Import Intercompany Transactions | FUN_INTERFACE_BATCHES, FUN_INTERFACE_HEADERS, FUN_INTERFACE_DIST_LINES, FUN_INTERFACE_BATCHDISTS | FUN_INTERFACE_REJECTIONS | Intercompany Transactions > Import Errors tab, or Tasks > Correct Import Errors |
| Import Journals | GL_INTERFACE | GL_INTERFACE (STATUS) and GL_JE_ERROR_CODES | Import Errors tab of the General Accounting dashboard > Correct Journal Import Data spreadsheet |
| Load and Import Bank Statement; Import Bank Statement from a Spreadsheet | CE_STATEMENT_HEADERS_INT, CE_STATEMENT_LINES_INT | CE_STMT_IMPORT_ERRORS | Correct and reload |
| Import External Transactions to the Tax Repository | ZX_TRANSACTION, ZX_TRANSACTION_LINES, ZX_TAX_LINES_INTERFACE | ZX_IMPORT_ERRORS | Correct and reload |

Triage the rejected rows of one load request through a BI Publisher data model (sections 8 and 9). The joins follow the documented column meanings; they are not declared foreign keys.

```sql
-- Payables invoice import rejections for one load request
SELECT i.invoice_num, i.vendor_num, i.source, i.status,
       r.parent_table, r.reject_lookup_code, r.rejection_message
FROM   ap_invoices_interface i
JOIN   ap_interface_rejections r
       ON  r.parent_table = 'AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE'
       AND r.parent_id    = i.invoice_id
WHERE  i.load_request_id = :p_load_request_id;

-- AutoInvoice validation errors for one load request
SELECT l.batch_source_name, l.trx_number, ae.message_text, ae.invalid_value
FROM   ra_interface_lines_all l
JOIN   ra_interface_errors_all ae ON ae.interface_line_id = l.interface_line_id
WHERE  l.load_request_id = :p_load_request_id;

-- Purchasing document import errors for one load request
SELECT h.document_num, h.process_code, pe.table_name, pe.column_name, pe.error_message
FROM   po_headers_interface h
JOIN   po_interface_errors pe ON pe.interface_header_id = h.interface_header_id
WHERE  h.load_request_id = :p_load_request_id;
```

### 7.4 ERP Integration Service

The ERP Integration Service automates bulk inbound and outbound flows: file upload to UCM, ESS job submission, status tracking, callbacks and notifications. It supersedes the Financial Utilities Service, which is deprecated and shouldn't be used by new customers.

| Interface | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| SOAP | `https://<POD_HOST>/fscmService/ErpIntegrationService?WSDL`; QName `{http://xmlns.oracle.com/apps/financials/commonModules/shared/model/erpIntegrationService/}ErpIntegrationService` |
| REST actions | `POST /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations` with `OperationName` in the body |
| REST queries | `GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations?finder=<FINDER>;<VARIABLE>=<VALUE>` |
| REST item | `GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations/{OperationName}` |

| SOAP operation | REST form (documented) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| importBulkData | POST, `OperationName=importBulkData` | Upload a base64 zip to a UCM account, run Load Interface File for Import and the import job. `jobOptions` example: `InterfaceDetails=<ID>,ImportOption=Y,PurgeOption=Y,ExtractFileType=ALL`. |
| uploadFileToUcm | POST, `OperationName=uploadFileToUCM` | Upload only; returns the document ID. |
| submitESSJobRequest | POST, `OperationName=submitESSJobRequest` with `JobPackageName`, `JobDefName`, `ESSParameters` | Run any ESS job. Parameters in job order, `#NULL` for empty ones. Returns the request ID. |
| exportBulkData | POST, `OperationName=exportBulkData` | Run a job, then zip its output and log to UCM. For reports and outbound flows. |
| submitJobWithOutput | Not documented | Submit with callback. The Oracle Integration adapter guide says it will be deprecated; use exportBulkData. |
| getESSJobStatus | finder `ESSJobStatusRF;requestId=<ID>` | Status in `RequestStatus`, for example SUCCEEDED. |
| getESSExecutionDetails | finder `ESSExecutionDetailsRF;requestId=<ID>` | JSON tree of the job and its child jobs with statuses. |
| downloadESSJobExecutionDetails | finder `ESSJobExecutionDetailsRF;requestId=<ID>,fileType=<FILE_TYPE>` | Log and output files as a zip; file type LOG, OUT or ALL. |
| getDocumentIdsForFilePrefix, getDocumentForDocumentId | finders `DocumentIdsByFilePrefixRF`, `DocumentRF` | Find and download UCM files. |
| appendFileComment, confirmExtractConsumption | Not documented | Tag a file with a comment (prefix searches can exclude tagged files); confirm an extract was downloaded. |
| updateInterfaceData | Not documented | Upload corrected interface data for an import process and load request ID. |
| extractAndPurge | Not documented | Upload load and import logs to UCM and purge the interface tables. |
| loadAndImportData, downloadExportOutput | Not documented | Older operations; the guide points to importBulkData and downloadESSJobExecutionDetails. |

A complete REST example for a Payables invoice import (request body, submission, status polling and log download) is in 6.5.10.

Callbacks and job status:
- `NotificationCode`: first digit 1 = email, 2 = bell, 3 = both; second digit 0 = always, 1 = on success, 2 = on failure; `#NULL` = none. It applies to loadAndImportData, importBulkData, exportBulkData and extractAndPurge.
- `CallbackURL`: a web service you implement; Fusion sends it the job status when the job ends. `#NULL` means no callback.
- Oracle Integration: the ERP Cloud Adapter action Import Bulk Data into Oracle ERP Cloud with Enable Callback raises the ErpImportBulkDataEvent event, and a separate callback integration subscribes to it. The Financials event list also has ERP Integration Inbound and ERP Integration Outbound (7.8).
- ESS REST API (REST API for Common Features): `POST /ess/rest/scheduler/v1/requests` (body `jobDefinitionId`, `requestParameters`, optional `callbackSubscription` with `callbackUrlPrefix` and `callbackResourcePath`), `GET /ess/rest/scheduler/v1/requests/{requestId}`, `POST /ess/rest/scheduler/v1/requests/{requestId}/cancel`, `POST /ess/rest/scheduler/v1/requests/{requestId}/subscribe`.
- ERP ICS Integration Service (`ErpIcsIntegrationService`, operation getInboundProcesses) lists the FBDI processes registered with the FBDI framework.

### 7.5 ADFdi spreadsheets

ADF Desktop Integration workbooks, their installation, usage rules and the mass-entry workbooks (for example Create Invoice in Spreadsheet and the procurement spreadsheet actions) are described in 5.4. ### 7.7 Scheduled processes per step

Submit and monitor processes in Navigator > Tools > Scheduled Processes > Schedule New Process; many also start from work-area task panes. A process set runs several processes in a defined order. Statuses include Blocked (an incompatible process is running), Wait, Ready, Running, Paused, Hold, Succeeded, Warning, Error, Error Auto-Retry, Error Manual Recovery, Validation Failed, Canceling, Canceled, Expired and Schedule Ended (20 values in the 26D scheduled-process guides). Frequency source: [E] Oracle scheduled-process guide, [U] Oracle Using or Implementing guide, [P] common practice, verify in your pod.

### 7.8 Business events and outbound integration

A public business event signals a business occurrence and carries a payload. Subscribers use the Oracle ERP Cloud Adapter in Oracle Integration (OIC) and call a REST or SOAP callback service for details. Enable each event that isn't on by default.

| Area | Events | Enable by | Callback or payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| Payables | Payables Invoice Created, Payables Invoice Approved, Payables Invoice Canceled, Payables Invoice Validated, Invoice Hold Applied, Invoice Hold Released, Payables Payment Created, Payables Payment Voided | Profile option AP: Enable Business Events, site level | Raised from UI and REST only, not from Import Payables Invoices or SOAP |
| Payments | Payment File Created | Profile option IBY: Enable Business Events, site level | Raised when a payment file completes |
| Procurement | Purchase Order Event (created, changed, finally closed, reopened), Supplier Created Event, Supplier Updated Event, Supplier Negotiation Invitation Event | Purchase Order Event is enabled by default | PurchaseOrderService getPurchaseOrder (SOAP, 7.6); no callback service listed for the supplier and negotiation events |
| Receiving | Create Receiving Receipt Event, Create Deliver Transaction Event, Create Return Transaction Event, Create Correction Transaction Event, ASN Creation Event, ASN Cancellation Event, Create Inbound ASN, Cancel Inbound ASN, Outbound Receipt Advice, Receipt Advice Event Notification | Adapter subscription | ReceiptService, ReceivingTransactionService, InboundShipmentService, ReceiptAdviceService |
| Order Management | Sales Order Notification, Order Status Updated, Sales Order Trade Compliance Screening, Sales Order Transportation Planning | Setup and Maintenance > Manage Business Event Trigger Points, for example Fulfillment Line Status Update | DocumentService getSalesOrderNotificationDetails; EventEnrichmentService getEnrichmentDetails; OrderFulfillmentRequestService getOrderFulfillmentRequestDetails. A trigger point can instead publish to a connector set up on Manage Connector Details |
| Shipping and inventory | Shipment Advice Event, Advanced Shipment Notice Event, Outbound Shipment Request, Shipment Request Generate Event, Backorder Line Event, Pick Confirm Event, Manifest Request Event, Trade Screening Request Event, Transfer Price Published Event, Standard Cost Published Event | Adapter subscription; several are published by scheduled processes (7.7) | ShipmentService, ShipmentLineService |
| Receivables | Receivables Invoice Completed, Receivables Invoice Incompleted, Receivables Invoice Paid, Receivables Credit Memo Completed, Receivables Credit Memo Incompleted, Receivables Credit Memo Applied, Receivables Autoinvoice Completed, Receivables Lockbox Batch Completed, Standard Receipt Created, Standard Receipt Applied, Standard Receipt Unapplied, Standard Receipt Reversed, Standard Receipt Deleted, Credit Case Folder Created, Credit Case Folder Refresh Requested | ERP Business Events REST API | Credit Case Folder Closure is also published; one adapter guide version lists it as enabled by default (verify in your pod) |
| Advanced Collections | Strategy Closed, Strategy External Task Opened | Feature Automatically Initiate or Fulfill Collections Tasks in Third Party Systems | External collections task systems |
| Revenue Management | Revenue Contract Batch Created (RevenueContractBatchCreated), raised by Identify Customer Contracts | Feature Generate Public Events on Revenue Contract Batch Created (Using Revenue Management); the adapter guide lists the ERP Business Events REST API | REST Revenue Contracts; payload Request ID, Job Name, Business Context (Contract Creation) |
| General Ledger and common | Accounting Period Opened, Accounting Period Closed, Accounting Period Reopened, Journal Batch Approved, Journal Batch Posting Completed; ERP Integration Inbound, ERP Integration Outbound | ERP Business Events REST API; ERP Integrations REST API | Bulk import and export completion (7.4) |

Enable a Financials event through REST:
- `GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpBusinessEvents` lists events with `BusinessEventCode`, `BusinessEventIdentifier` and `EnabledFlag`.
- `PATCH /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpBusinessEvents/{ErpBusinessEventId}` with body `{"EnabledFlag": true}`.

ERP Cloud Adapter facts that shape designs:
- Trigger (event) connections must use the Username Password Token policy; an OAuth trigger connection can't receive Fusion events.
- Uploads to UCM of up to 1 GB are possible, but unzip or virus scan can still fail on Fusion size limits. Downloads from UCM aren't supported.
- The adapter can't run SQL; query through a BI Publisher report (section 8).
- Custom business events can be defined in ERP Cloud and subscribed to.
- Outbound bulk data: exportBulkData for BI Publisher jobs with callback (7.4) and BICC extracts (section 8). The Business Objects guides (bo_fin, bo_proc, bo_scm) describe read-optimized business views for extraction, for example payablesInvoiceTransactionsExtract; they document data, not events.

### 7.9 Decision guide

| Need | Use | Why and limits |
|---|---|---|
| One record, entered or fixed by a person | UI (section 5) | Full validation, approvals and attachments |
| Tens to a few thousand rows by a business user | ADFdi workbook where one exists (5.4; correction workbooks 7.5) | Interactive validation and row status; needs the Excel add-in |
| Conversion or recurring high-volume load | FBDI (7.1 to 7.3) | Built for large volumes; asynchronous; errors kept in interface tables; no PO updates; 10,000-distribution limit per purchasing document |
| Automate FBDI or run any ESS job from outside | erpintegrations REST or ErpIntegrationService (7.4) | One call for upload, load and import; callback or event at completion |
| Create, read or update one document in real time | REST (section 6) | Raises Payables events; first choice when a resource exists |
| Operation without a suitable REST resource, or where Oracle recommends SOAP | SOAP (7.6) | Example: PO changes with PurchaseOrderServiceV2; check the deprecation status first |
| React to a change in Fusion | Business events with OIC (7.8) | A signal per occurrence; enrich through the callback service; enable the event first |
| Outbound bulk data or reports | exportBulkData, BI Publisher, BICC (section 8) | Don't page through transactional REST resources for bulk extraction |
| Recurring processing inside Fusion | Scheduled processes and process sets (7.7) | Respect incompatibilities and recommended frequencies |
| Actions by an AI agent (sections 10, 11) | REST for reads and single writes; erpintegrations for bulk, with human approval of each write | Same security and audit as the human channels (section 12) |

## 8. Reporting and analytics (OTBI, BI Publisher, BICC, FDI)

Fusion has five reporting and extraction layers. They differ in data latency, in how they apply security and in who can build content. Use this section together with section 9 (SQL cookbook), section 6 (REST), section 7 (FBDI, SOAP, scheduled processes) and section 12 (security). The 26D guides call BI Publisher "Oracle Analytics Publisher"; this section uses both names.

| Tool | Reads from | Latency | Security applied | Typical P2P and O2C use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTBI (Oracle Transactional Business Intelligence) | Subject areas mapped to ADF view objects and their tables | Real time | Same function and data security as the application pages | Ad hoc analyses, dashboards, infolets, operational lists (holds, open POs, unapplied cash) |
| BI Publisher (Oracle Analytics Publisher) | Data models: SQL on Fusion tables, OTBI analyses, other sources | Real time | Catalog permissions; SQL data sets are not data-secured (8.2.6) | Formatted documents, predefined close reports, bursting, file outputs |
| BICC (Business Intelligence Cloud Connector) | Public view objects (data stores) | Batch, full or incremental | BICC console and storage roles; treat output as unrestricted bulk data | Bulk feeds to a warehouse or data lake |
| Data Extraction tool | Business views and user-defined queries on a replicated read-optimized store | Near real-time replica, batch or on-demand extracts | Custom job role; OAuth for REST | Oracle's long-term replacement for BICC and Publisher-based extraction |
| FDI (Oracle Fusion Data Intelligence) | Prebuilt pipelines into Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse, analysed in Oracle Analytics Cloud | Scheduled incremental refresh | Separate FDI subscription and security | KPIs, history, cross-pillar analytics, ML predictions |

### 8.1 OTBI

#### 8.1.1 Concept

- OTBI is the real-time, self-service reporting layer. The BI Server builds physical SQL from metadata that maps subject areas to ADF view objects and their database tables. The Presentation Server formats the result.
- A subject area holds one fact folder (numeric measures) and several dimension folders (attributes such as dates, IDs and text, BI-enabled flexfield segments, and hierarchies such as Year, Quarter, Month).
- To combine subject areas in one analysis, use columns only from dimension folders common to all of them (at least one) and include one fact column from each subject area.
- The catalog is organized as Shared Folders > product family > product, for example Shared Folders > Financials > Payables. Save new or copied content in Shared Folders > Custom (preserved across updates) or My Folders (private). You can't change folder or object permissions on predefined catalog content, and changes saved outside Custom can be lost during updates; for predefined reports use Customize (8.2.1). Don't store anything in the predefined Temp folder in My Folders; Publisher uses it and purges it automatically every 24 hours.
- Flexfield segments appear in subject areas only after they are BI-enabled and the scheduled process Import Oracle Fusion Data Extensions for Transactional Business Intelligence has run.

#### 8.1.2 Build an analysis

1. Open the Reports and Analytics work area (Navigator > Tools > Reports and Analytics; verify in your pod) or the Reports and Analytics panel tab of a work area.
2. Click Create > Analysis, select a subject area and click Continue. This starts the wizard. For advanced features (dashboards, catalog management, links to application pages), click Browse Catalog.
3. Select Columns: expand folders and pick columns. Interaction Default or Drill adds the next hierarchy level; Navigate to Transaction opens the source record but needs extra link configuration; None turns off drilling; Hidden keeps a column for filters only. Use Add/Remove Subject Areas to combine subject areas.
4. Select Views: table, graph or both. A graph needs at least one fact column.
5. Edit Table or Edit Graph: layout options Columns, Prompt For, Section By and Excluded.
6. Sort and Filter, then Highlight (numeric thresholds). Turn on Preview to check the data.
7. Save: enter a name, choose a folder under Shared Folders > Custom and click Submit.
8. Optionally add the analysis to a dashboard, an infolet or the Reports and Analytics panel tab of a work area, or deliver it on a schedule with an agent.

#### 8.1.3 Security

| Layer | Mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Subject area access | Transaction Analysis Duty roles (OBI roles, role codes start with FBI_), for example Payables Invoice Transaction Analysis Duty | Each inherits BI Consumer Role. A custom job role needs both the OBI and the Financials version of the duty (for example Fixed Asset Transaction Analysis Duty and Fixed Asset Transaction Analysis). Predefined Transaction Analysis Duty roles can't be copied or modified. |
| Data security | Data security policies and security profiles granted through the Transaction Analysis Duty roles (business unit, ledger, inventory organization and so on) | Oracle: OTBI data "is secured in a similar way to the data that's returned in application pages." Analyses fail if the user can't access every subject area in the analysis. |
| Authoring | BI Consumer Role (run), BI Author Role (create and edit; inherits BI Consumer Role), BI Administrator Role (superuser; inherits BI Author Role) | Predefined Financials job roles that inherit a Transaction Analysis Duty are assigned BI Author Role by default. None of the predefined Financials job roles inherits BI Administrator Role; Oracle recommends provisioning it in a test environment only. |
| Catalog folders | Folder reporting duty roles, for example Financials Folder Reporting Duty, Procurement Folder Reporting Duty, Supply Chain Management Folder Reporting Duty; all users hold Custom BI Web cat Reporting Duty | To hide predefined folders, build a custom role based on Custom BI Web cat Reporting Duty, run Import User and Role Application Security Data, then Browse Catalog > Administration > Reload Files and Metadata. |

#### 8.1.4 OTBI from integrations and agents

- The 26D Financials REST API documents the `analytics` resource: `GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/analytics`, `GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/analytics/{analyticsUniqID}` and `POST /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/analytics/action/executeLogicalQuery`. The action takes a list of BI Logical SQL requests, each with a request identifier and a query, plus an optional asynchronous option, and returns results grouped by request identifier. Because it queries OTBI, expect the caller's OTBI roles and data security to apply (verify in your pod). This gives an agent a direct, secured read path (sections 6 and 11).
- In BI Publisher, a data set of type Oracle BI Analysis reuses an OTBI analysis, so the report inherits the subject area security of the user who runs it (verify in your pod).

```sql
-- Body query for POST /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/analytics/action/executeLogicalQuery
-- Copy real folder and column names from an analysis built in the UI (verify in your pod).
SELECT
  "<DIMENSION_FOLDER>"."<ATTRIBUTE_COLUMN>" s_1,
  "<FACT_FOLDER>"."<MEASURE_COLUMN>" s_2
FROM "Payables Invoices - Installments Real Time"
WHERE "<DIMENSION_FOLDER>"."<FILTER_COLUMN>" = '<VALUE>'
FETCH FIRST 500 ROWS ONLY
```

### 8.2 BI Publisher (Oracle Analytics Publisher)

#### 8.2.1 Building blocks

| Object | Holds | P2P and O2C examples |
|---|---|---|
| Data model | Data sets (SQL Query, Oracle BI Analysis, View Object, Web Service, HTTP XML feed, Excel, XML, CSV, LDAP, MDX), parameters, lists of values, bursting definitions | Open AP installments; customer statement data |
| Layout | RTF (Template Builder for Word), Excel, PDF form, eText for character-delimited or fixed-position files such as EFT and EDI, XSL | Remittance advice, dunning letters, bank files |
| Report | One or more layouts, a data model reference and properties; optional style templates and subtemplates | Predefined close reports (8.5); custom reports under Shared Folders > Custom |
| Job definition | Scheduled process wrapper (job type BIPJobType) | Lets users submit a custom report from Scheduled Processes (8.2.4) |

- Create content from Reports and Analytics > Browse Catalog > New. Creating or editing data models needs BI Publisher Data Model Developer Role ("Creates and edits Business Intelligence Publisher data models"). It is inherited by Application Developer, which Application Implementation Consultant inherits in turn.
- SQL data sets run against the Fusion schema through provisioned data sources: ApplicationDB_FSCM for Financials data, ApplicationDB_CRM and ApplicationDB_HCM. These names come from the Fusion Applications 11.1.7 Data Modeling Guide; Procurement and SCM tables are normally queried through ApplicationDB_FSCM as well (verify in your pod).
- To change a predefined report, use Customize. It copies the report, folder structure and permissions to Custom and links the copy to the original. For a predefined data model, copy it into Custom and point the custom report at the copy.
- Oracle's SaaS best practices: the 26D Financials guide points to My Oracle Support document 2145444.1. The following come from the 2016 white paper version and may have changed (verify in your pod): select only needed columns, filter with WHERE clauses and bind parameters, avoid inline queries per row and PL/SQL functions in WHERE clauses, avoid binding more than 100 values to one parameter, keep queries under the default 600-second query timeout, and schedule reports that run longer than 10 minutes instead of running them online.

#### 8.2.2 SQL data model on Appendix A tables

The example lists open AP installments and restricts rows to business units assigned to the user running the report. Section 9 has more patterns.

```sql
-- Data set OPEN_AP_INSTALLMENTS (SQL Query, data source ApplicationDB_FSCM)
SELECT aia.ORG_ID,
       pz.SEGMENT1               AS supplier_number,
       hp.PARTY_NAME             AS supplier_name,
       aia.INVOICE_NUM,
       aia.INVOICE_CURRENCY_CODE,
       aps.PAYMENT_NUM,
       aps.DUE_DATE,
       aps.AMOUNT_REMAINING
FROM   AP_INVOICES_ALL aia
JOIN   AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL aps ON aps.INVOICE_ID = aia.INVOICE_ID
JOIN   POZ_SUPPLIERS pz              ON pz.VENDOR_ID  = aia.VENDOR_ID
JOIN   HZ_PARTIES hp                 ON hp.PARTY_ID   = pz.PARTY_ID
WHERE  aia.CANCELLED_DATE IS NULL
AND    aps.AMOUNT_REMAINING <> 0
AND    aps.DUE_DATE <= :P_AS_OF_DATE
-- Row filter: business units assigned to the user who runs the report.
-- This approximates Fusion data security; it is not the same check (verify in your pod).
AND    EXISTS (SELECT 1
               FROM   FUN_USER_ROLE_DATA_ASGNMNTS urda
               WHERE  urda.USER_GUID = (<USER_GUID_FOR_XDO_USER_NAME>)
               AND    urda.ORG_ID = aia.ORG_ID
               AND    urda.ACTIVE_FLAG = 'Y')
-- Optional inside the subquery: AND urda.ROLE_NAME IN (<ROLE_CODE_LIST>)
```

- `FUN_USER_ROLE_DATA_ASGNMNTS` holds user, role and data security context assignments (Appendix A). USER_GUID identifies the user in Oracle Identity Management, ORG_ID is the business unit and ACTIVE_FLAG = 'Y' marks an active assignment (column comments).
- `<USER_GUID_FOR_XDO_USER_NAME>` is a scalar subquery that returns the USER_GUID of the login in `:xdo_user_name`. The user account table it needs is documented in the Tables and Views for HCM guide, outside the catalogs used for this document (verify in your pod).
- A ready-to-use alternative that matches on the user name directly, through `FUN_USER_BO_DATA_ASSIGNMENTS_V` (USERNAME, DATASEC_CONTEXT_TYPE_CODE 'ORA_BU_ID'), is the BU data-access predicate in 9.1; it needs no HCM user table. Use the same predicate across reports.
- `:xdo_user_name` is a Publisher system variable that holds the user who submits the report. Use the same filter in the business unit parameter's list of values so users can only pick their own business units.

#### 8.2.3 Bursting

A bursting definition is part of the data model:

- Split By: the element that splits the data, for example supplier or customer ID. The data set must be sorted or grouped by it.
- Deliver By: the element that drives formatting and delivery; often the same element.
- Delivery Query: SQL that returns, for each key, the template, output format, locale and delivery channel and destination.

P2P and O2C uses: remittance advice per supplier, statements and dunning letters per customer, report packs per business unit. Delivery channels such as email or FTP must be set up by a BI administrator (verify in your pod).

#### 8.2.4 Scheduling

| Option | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Publisher scheduler | Open the report and click Schedule; monitor in Report Job History (verify in your pod) | For custom reports without a job definition |
| Scheduled process (ESS) | Setup and Maintenance > Application Extensions functional area > Manage Enterprise Scheduler Job Definitions and Job Sets for Financial, Supply Chain Management, and Related Applications > Manage Job Definitions tab > Create. Job Application Name FscmEss, Job Type BIPJobType (no other type), Report ID `Custom/<FAMILY>/<PRODUCT>/<REPORT>.xdo` including the .xdo extension, plus parameters | Creates a privilege with code RUN_<JOB_DEFINITION_NAME> and name "Run <display name>"; assign it to roles in the Security Console. Users then submit from Scheduled Processes, with process sets and recurrence (section 7). If the task is missing, enable the Enterprise Scheduler Job Definitions and Job Sets feature for the offering. |
| Predefined Financials reports | Scheduled Processes > Schedule New Process | Most close reports in 8.5 |

#### 8.2.5 Run reports from integrations

| Interface | Endpoint, relative to `https://<POD_HOST>` | Use |
|---|---|---|
| ExternalReportWSSService, operation runReport (protected; credentials in the SOAP header) | `/xmlpserver/services/ExternalReportWSSService?wsdl` | Oracle recommends the protected services when a synchronous call is needed. Output is always a base64-encoded string; response attachments aren't supported, so MTOM doesn't apply. Keep it for short, small reports within the integration payload limits. |
| ScheduleReportWSSService, operation getDocumentData | `/xmlpserver/services/ScheduleReportWSSService?wsdl` | Fetch output of a scheduled job |
| ReportService runReport and ScheduleService getDocumentData (public; credentials in the payload) | `/xmlpserver/services/v2/ReportService?wsdl`, `/xmlpserver/services/v2/ScheduleService?wsdl` | Same functions with credentials in the body |
| Large or long reports | Wrap the report in a custom job definition; submit with ErpIntegrationService exportBulkData or `POST /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/erpintegrations` (ExportBulkData); with EnableEvent=Y; output goes to UCM; react to ExportBulkDataEvent (it carries the documentId) or a callback; download with the UCM GenericSoapService GET_FILE command | Oracle's asynchronous pattern for long-running or large reports (section 7) |
| Publisher REST API | `.../services/rest/v1/reports/{reportPath}/run` (multipart; URL-encoded report path) | Documented for Oracle Analytics Cloud and Oracle Analytics Server, not in the Fusion 26D guides (verify in your pod) |

#### 8.2.6 Security considerations

Oracle states that a data model with physical SQL can either select directly from tables, "in which case the data you return isn't subject to data-security restrictions", or join to secured list views, in which case the user's security profiles decide the rows. Personally identifiable information tables stay protected by virtual private database policies, also for Publisher reports. A Financials report built on `AP_INVOICES_ALL` therefore returns every business unit unless you filter it.

| Mitigation | How |
|---|---|
| Few data model authors | Oracle: "Because you can create data models on unsecured data, you're recommended to minimize the number of users who can create data models." Limit BI Publisher Data Model Developer Role (and Application Developer, which inherits it), above all in production. |
| Secured sources first | Use OTBI subject areas or Oracle BI Analysis data sets; join secured list views where they exist |
| Explicit row filters | Filter by the running user's assignments as in 8.2.2, and test with users who have different access |
| Catalog permissions | Keep data models and reports in dedicated Custom folders; grant run access through an existing or custom role, not to everyone |
| Controlled outputs | Review bursting destinations and scheduled report recipients; outputs leave Fusion security |
| Agents | Expose parameterized reports to an agent through an integration user (section 11), never a free-form SQL data model |

### 8.3 BICC (Business Intelligence Cloud Connector)

#### 8.3.1 What it is

- BICC extracts business intelligence and other data in bulk to external storage. It is part of the Oracle Applications Cloud subscription. Sign in at `https://<POD_HOST>/biacm`.
- Access: create a role (for example BIACM_ADMIN, category BI - Abstract Roles) with ESS Administrator Role and ORA_ASM_APPLICATION_IMPLEMENTATION_ADMIN_ABSTRACT, or assign BI Administrator Role. For extract files on UCM, create a role (for example BICC_UCM_CONTENT_ADMIN) with OBIA_EXTRACTTRANSFORMLOAD_RWD; files sit in the OBIAImport security group.
- A data store is a public view object (PVO). Its page in the Extract Data Stores guides (Financials, Procurement, SCM) gives the Data Store Key, Primary Keys, Initial Extract Date column, Incremental Extract Date column and attributes. For example, Payables Invoices has PK ApInvoicesInvoiceId, initial column ApInvoicesCreationDate and incremental column ApInvoicesLastUpdateDate. Lineage spreadsheets on Oracle Cloud Customer Connect map PVO attributes to the tables and columns in Appendix A.
- Offerings group data stores. You can create offerings, add data stores, select columns and add filters written as `__DATASTORE__.<BI_VO_COLUMN_NAME>`.

The full Data Store Key is the prefix, a dot and the PVO name from 8.3.3, for example `FscmTopModelAM.FinExtractAM.ApBiccExtractAM.InvoiceHeaderExtractPVO`.
